title: Low Fraud Score IP: How to Get One and Keep It
author: IP Ready
excerpt: A low fraud score is rented trust. What the 0–100 number actually measures, which IP types start lowest, and the habits that keep the number down for months.
body:
Anyone shopping for IPs eventually meets the phrase 'low fraud score' — seller listings advertise it, buyers test for it, and marketplaces build it into account onboarding. But the score is not a property of the address itself. It is a snapshot of how a scoring service currently reads it, which means it can be chosen well, and it can be kept well. This guide covers both: how to acquire an address that starts low, and the maintenance that stops it drifting back up.

What the Number Actually Measures

Every fraud-score service blends roughly the same signal groups into a 0–100 read:

  • Blacklist presence — current and historical appearances on spam and abuse databases.
  • Network type — hosting and datacenter ASNs score worse than consumer ISP lines; the address's registered owner matters as much as its behavior.
  • Anonymizer detection — whether the address currently behaves like, or is known as, a VPN/proxy/Tor exit.
  • Abuse recency — reports decay with time; a clean record three months old reads better than a clean record from last week.
  • Consistency — registered geography, routing, and timezone that agree with each other.

One caveat worth internalizing: providers weight these differently, so the same address can score 12 on one service and 60 on another. Scores are directional. When a purchase decision hangs on one, check it on more than one service before you commit.

Which IP Types Start Lowest

TypeTypical starting scoreThe catch
Static residential (ISP)Lowest — a consumer ISP line registered to you aloneCosts more; quality depends on the provider's sourcing
Mobile (4G/5G)Low — carriers are highly trustedShared by thousands; scores swing with strangers' behavior
Clean dedicated datacenterMedium — usable but flagged as hostingNever reaches residential trust, no matter how clean
Rotating residential poolsA lottery per requestYou inherit whatever the last user of that exit did

The pattern is simple: exclusivity beats type. A modest line that only you use will outscore a prestigious range that a hundred strangers also call home.

How to Get One

Buy on reputation, not price. Ask the seller directly for the abuse history of the specific range you will receive — providers that keep clean sourcing answer easily, and the ones that dodge are answering too. If a deal is far below the market rate for static residential, the discount is usually coming from address quality.

Test before you commit. Reputable providers offer trials precisely so you can verify. Run the exit through a risk scan, check it on a second scoring service, and look at the signals rather than only the headline number: 'score 10, but flagged as proxy' will still cause friction on strict platforms.

Prefer dedicated over shared wherever the budget allows. The premium for a dedicated static residential line is, in effect, a payment to not inherit other people's behavior.

How to Keep It Low

  • Warm it up. A fresh address that immediately runs high-volume automation recreates the exact pattern fraud models watch for. Light, ordinary-looking activity for the first days builds a baseline that protects you later.
  • One address, one job. Mixing scraping bursts and account sessions on the same exit is the fastest way to spend its reputation. Segregate by risk: account traffic on your clean line, dirty work on throwaway infrastructure.
  • Keep the story consistent. Timezone, language, and login geography should agree with the address's registered location. Consistency reads as human; drift reads as a hijacked session.
  • Re-scan on a schedule. Reputation databases update continuously, and scores move even when you do nothing. A weekly scan catches drift while it is still cheap to fix — and a scan before any session that matters, not after something breaks.

A low score is not bought once; it is maintained like any other asset. Run a scan on your current exit to see where it stands, or check a whole list at once with the batch checker before committing to a purchase. For the full maintenance routine, see how to lower your IP risk score.
